subject.title: [Feature]: Add bounded/validated append semantics for pre-compaction memory flush

question: Should OpenClaw make canonical daily-memory memory-flush writes fail closed by default with built-in size/scaffold/dedupe checks, or should that stricter behavior wait behind a new opt-in/plugin API?
rationale: Current main lacks the requested guardrails, but changing the flush boundary affects existing memory prompts and the optional validator-hook idea crosses a security boundary that automation should not choose alone.

options.title: Land narrow built-in guard
options.body: Use the existing wrapper boundary to reject oversized/scaffold daily-memory appends and skip duplicates, without adding a command-style validator hook.

options.title: Require opt-in strict mode
options.body: Keep current append-only behavior by default and require a new explicit config/API surface for bounded daily-memory enforcement.

options.title: Defer to plugin API design
options.body: Leave this issue open for a broader plugin-owned validation-hook design before accepting any stricter runtime behavior.

recommendation.title: Land narrow built-in guard
recommendation.body: Use the existing wrapper boundary to reject oversized/scaffold daily-memory appends and skip duplicates, without adding a command-style validator hook.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced the memory-flush feature and has the clearest history signal for deciding the default product contract.
